description: The Uptime Institute's Annual Outage Analysis is a yearly report on the frequency, causes, severity and cost of IT and data-centre outages, drawn from Uptime's annual global surveys of data-centre operators and IT managers, its database of publicly reported outages, and member information. The 2025 edition finds that overall outage frequency and severity declined for the fourth year in a row, that power problems remain the most common cause of serious and severe data-centre outages, that IT and network causes and failures of staff to follow procedures are growing, that cyber-security incidents are rising and severe, and that 54 percent of surveyed operators said their latest significant outage cost more than 100,000 US dollars, one in five more than 1 million. The Uptime Institute, an advisory and certification body for data centres, publishes it to track resilience trends. Coverage: worldwide, respondents from all regions, annual editions since about 2020. Format and access: the executive summary is a free PDF after filling in a form, a webinar presents the results, and the full report is in the Uptime Intelligence subscription library with a free four-week evaluation. Caveats: survey-based and self-reported, not a complete outage register; public-outage counts depend on media coverage; the full report is paywalled. Simulation uses: event statistics and cause distributions for resilience and cascading-failure models of data centres, and hazard exposure to power grid and weather events. Related records: the OVHcloud fire case study and the Facebook 2021 outage give single events; ENISA telecom incident reports cover networks.
